newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
The chief inspector of schools, Chris Woodhead has ordered an urgent inquiry into school funding after shocking revelations that there is an acute shortage of books in British schools.
NURSING HOME FIRMS FACE HARDER SQUEEZER

The nursing home sector is expected to face a difficult year following budget commitments to limit the amount of money that local councils can spend on elderly care. A report by healthcare consultants Laing & Buisson, which claims that Kenneth Clarke's budget will leave councils between 110 million and 130 milllion stg short, follows a poor performance in the care sector during 1996.
The yen has slipped to a four year low following concern over Japanese economic weakness.
GREENALLS SQUARES UP FOR THE NEXT CENTURY
Pub and leisure giant Greenalls is to invest 60m stg on managed theme pubs and the expansion of its Village Leisure fitness hotels.
